frontmatter.seoTitle: Aspose.Note How to Save Notebooks Python
frontmatter.title: How to Save Notebooks Python

blocks.content: Developers need to save or export notebooks created with Aspose.Note to specific formats such as PDF or image files using Python. The `aspose_note_foss` package provides the core classes and methods required to perform this operation programmatically in Python note-taking workflows.
Aspose.Note -- Required installation and a loaded document/workbook.
For details on prerequisites, see the Aspose.Note documentation.

Aspose.Note enables saving notebooks and individual notes in Python using the `Notebook` and `Document` classes. The output format is determined by the file extension provided in the save path, supporting common formats such as PDF, HTML, and image formats.

To save a notebook, instantiate `Notebook` with the source file, then call `save()` with the desired output path. For individual notes, use `Document` instead. The `save()` method accepts a file path and optional `SaveOptions` to control export behavior like image resolution or PDF compliance level.

When specifying the output path, ensure the file extension matches the target format—`.pdf` for PDF, `.html` for HTML, or `.png`/`.jpg` for images. Aspose.Note automatically selects the appropriate exporter based on the extension.

This section demonstrates how to save notebooks using Aspose.Note in Python. It covers loading an existing notebook, making a simple modification, and saving the result to disk. The example uses the canonical import path and follows the API surface for Aspose.Note.

import aspose_note_foss

# Load an existing notebook
notebook = aspose_note_foss.Notebook("input.one")

# Save the notebook to a new file
notebook.save("output.one")

Aspose.Note supports saving notebooks to common output formats including PDF, HTML, and image formats such as PNG and JPEG. Format selection is controlled via the `SaveFormat` enumeration passed to the `Document.save()` method.

items: PDF: High-fidelity document export suitable for sharing and printing
HTML: Web-compatible export preserving text and basic formatting
PNG/JPEG: Raster image output for visual documentation or integration
